findings.description: AWS access key and secret access key are embedded in plaintext within the EC2 user_data script, exposing long-lived credentials to anyone with access to the instance metadata service, console, or Terraform state.

The security group allows inbound SSH (port 22) from 0.0.0.0/0, exposing the management port to the entire internet and enabling brute-force or credential-stuffing attacks, especially since the instance sits in a subnet with public IP assignment enabled.

The security group allows inbound HTTP (port 80) from 0.0.0.0/0 with no compensating controls (e.g., WAF, TLS termination), exposing an unauthenticated web service directly to the internet in cleartext.
The EBS volume does not enable the encrypted attribute, leaving data at rest unencrypted and vulnerable to exposure if the underlying storage or snapshots are accessed improperly.
The EBS snapshot inherits the unencrypted state of its source volume, meaning snapshot data (which can be shared or copied) is also stored without encryption.

map_public_ip_on_launch is set to true, automatically assigning public IPs to instances launched in this subnet. This is the subnet used by aws_instance.web_host, which combined with the open SSH/HTTP security group directly increases internet-facing attack surface for that host.

map_public_ip_on_launch is set to true, causing any instance launched in this subnet to receive a public IP address by default, expanding the network attack surface unnecessarily. No instance currently uses this subnet, so severity is lower than web_subnet.

findings.issue_category: missing encryption and public access controls
findings.description: The S3 bucket storing VPC flow logs has no server-side encryption configuration and no public access block or bucket policy restricting access, risking unauthorized access to sensitive network traffic logs.
